task.description: Fresh, full re-scan of the reworked REQ-230 design artefact for any remaining disguised executable Elixir code, independent of CODE-DESIGNER's own claimed fix, plus re-confirmation that all previously-passed checks (AC1-AC7 traceability, precedent citations, security-invariant statements, scope boundaries) are unchanged.

result.note:
Independent fresh scan (not limited to the two originally-flagged spots) confirms the document is now clean. Grepped the entire file for `Enum.`, `fn `, `def `, `defp `, `defmodule`, `case `, `cond `, `with `, `|>` -- every hit is either inert English prose ('case match', 'in that case', 'is loaded', etc.) or inside a fenced block, and every fenced block (all 11 code fences, lines 166-173/189-206/262-273/282-287/382-385/399-402/426-429/438-441/453-464/617-623/635-637) contains only @type/@spec declarations, no function bodies. No `defmodule`, `def`, `defp`, `cond`, or real Enum.* pipe/call with executable predicate or accumulator logic remains anywhere.

Originally-flagged spot 1 (was line 312, Enum.filter(& &1.queried)): now reads as pure prose at current lines 312-316 ('keep only the subset whose `queried` flag is `true`, and build one allowlist entry per kept field') -- no Elixir syntax, confirmed clean.
Originally-flagged spot 2 (was line 489, Enum.reduce fn c, acc -> ... end): now reads as pure prose at current lines 489-495 ('starting from a `true` identity value, fold the list of per-clause fragments left-to-right, ANDing each successive clause's fragment onto the accumulator built so far') -- no `fn`, no `Enum.reduce`, no anonymous function, confirmed clean.

Additionally-fixed passages (CODE-DESIGNER's own re-scan findings) verified directly:
- §5.3 (lines 599-613): now leads with prose ('composes a reference to the resolved column... via ordinary Ecto.Query.dynamic/2 constructs. Conceptually, per operator: ...') with each Elixir-shaped fragment introduced by 'e.g.' inside parentheses -- matches the accepted case-arm/fragment-example precedent style exactly.
- §5.5 (lines 633-647): now leads with prose ('the result pairs the requested direction with a dynamic expression that simply references the resolved column') with the Elixir shape given only as a parenthetical 'e.g.' example -- same accepted framing.

All previously-assessed-sound items re-confirmed unchanged by this rework: AC1-AC7 traceability table (§10) intact and unchanged; Letflow.Engine.Expr.cmp_op() precedent citation unchanged (§0); the :json + queried:true forbidden-combination claim (Definition.Validator Rule 3, §0/§3.3 step 4) unchanged; entity_record_latest's typed-column table (§3.4) still matches the real schema in lib/letflow/entities/record/latest.ex; fragment/1 parameterisation discipline (§5.2) still binds both the JSONB key name and the comparison value as separate ^-bound parameters against a compile-time-fixed literal, never interpolated; §8's non-goals section still confirms no route/controller and no REQ-231 (cursor pagination/field-grant redaction) scope creep. The rework touched only the two originally-flagged passages and the two self-identified §5.3/§5.5 passages -- no other section's content changed in a way that alters any prior finding.

Verdict: PASS. Design is clean of implementation code and ready to proceed to ELIXIR-DEV.
